# Project for R Bio Data Science

## Introduction

In this project we will work with RNA-seq gene expression data from human macrophages, published by Alasoo et al. 2018 in Nature Genetics.

The macrophages were not taken directly from patients. Instead, induced stem cells from 84 healthy, unrelated donors in the HipSci collection, were differentiated into macrophages in the lab. Each donor's cells were exposed to four conditions: naive (untreated), IFNg (interferon-gamma for 18 hours), SL1344 (*Salmonella* infection for 5 hours) and IFNg_SL1344 (both treatments). Each donor contributes exactly one sample per condition and the dataset contains 336 samples in total.

The data consist of a count matrix with raw read counts for 35,033 genes across these samples and a metadata file that describes each sample, for example its donor, sex, condition and sequencing batch.

## Load Data

```{r}
#| eval: false
download.file(
  url      = "https://zenodo.org/records/259661/files/RNA_cqn_matrix.txt.gz?download=1",
  destfile = "data/_raw/RNA_cqn_matrix.txt.gz",
  mode     = "wb"
)

download.file(
  url      = "https://zenodo.org/records/259661/files/RNA_sample_metadata.txt.gz?download=1",
  destfile = "data/_raw/RNA_sample_metadata.txt.gz",
  mode     = "wb"
)

download.file(
  url      = "https://zenodo.org/records/259661/files/RNA_count_matrix.txt.gz?download=1",
  destfile = "data/_raw/RNA_count_matrix.txt.gz",
  mode     = "wb"
)
```

```{r}
library("tidyverse")

# sample meta data
sample_meta <- read_tsv("data/_raw/RNA_sample_metadata.txt.gz", show_col_types = FALSE)
write_tsv(x = sample_meta, file = "data/01_sample_meta_load.tsv")

# counts raw data
counts_raw_df <- read.delim("data/_raw/RNA_count_matrix.txt.gz", check.names = FALSE) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene_id")
write_tsv(x = counts_raw_df, file = "data/01_counts_raw_df_load.tsv")

# counts data normalized
counts_norm_df <- read.delim("data/_raw/RNA_cqn_matrix.txt.gz", check.names = FALSE) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene_id")
write_tsv(x = counts_norm_df, file = "data/01_counts_raw_df_load.tsv")
```

## Clean Data

### Sample metadata

#### Selection of columns

Selection of the relevant columns for analysis.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- sample_meta |>
  select(c("sample_id","donor","condition","replicate","condition_name","SL1344","IFNg"                  ,"received_as","mean_purity","max_purity", "sex","rna_concentration"                               ,"purity_bins"))

clean_sample_meta |>
  slice_sample(n = 10)
```

#### Dealing with NAs

First, a check is made to see which columns have NAs, after the previous selection

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))
```

All missing values were identified in columns related to sample purity. Before deciding how to handle these missing values, we investigated whether their occurrence followed any pattern. For example, if missing values were associated with specific donors, experimental conditions or other sample characteristics.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |> 
  filter(if_any(contains("purity"), is.na))
```

As we can see, there is a pattern: the NAs seemed to be grouped by the donor. From this information, the decision was taken to only delete the rows related to the donors that have no data about the purity of their samples. This way, we make sure that further analysis is made on reliable data.

But first, we need to filter the donors that follow this characteristic, and then remove them.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |> 
  group_by(donor) |> 
  select("donor",contains("purity")) |>
  filter(if_all(contains("purity"), is.na))
```

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta|>
  filter(!if_all(contains("purity"), is.na))

clean_sample_meta|>
  slice_sample(n=10)
```

```{r}
#clean_sample_meta |>
  #filter(if_any(everything(), is.na))

#clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta |>
  #drop_na()
```

#### Fixing columns naming

There are a couple of columns, with a odd name, specifically "SL1344", which refers to if it is a sample control or if the sample was infected with *Salmonella*; and also "IFNg", which refers if the sample was exposed to IFNγ (primed) or not (naive). Thus, the group decided to change this names for better understanding and consistency reasons.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta |>
  rename( 
    SL1344_infection = SL1344,
    IFNg_status = IFNg)

clean_sample_meta|>
  slice_sample(n=10)
```

#### Describing a cohort

```{r}
library("table1")

clean_sample_meta |>
  mutate(
    condition_name    = factor(condition_name),
    sex               = factor(sex),
    rna_concentration = factor(rna_concentration),
    received_as       = factor(received_as)
  ) |>
  table1(
    x = formula(~ sex + received_as + rna_concentration | condition_name),
    data = _
  )
```

From this cohort, we can observe one more inconsistency, only one variable across all conditions has the column "received_as" with a value of "alive/frozen". Logically, this sample characteristic should belong to a sample from the same donor. Thus, an investigation for this hypothesis was conducted.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |> 
  filter(received_as == "alive/frozen")

```

As we can see from the output, the samples from only one donor was received as alive/frozen. For consistency purposes, we decide to also remove the data from this donor.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta |>
 filter(!received_as == "alive/frozen")
```

Finally, we can export the cleaned sample metadata

```{r}
write_tsv(x = clean_sample_meta, file = "data/02_sample_meta_clean.tsv")
```

### Normalised Counts data

#### Filter low-count genes

The authors of the original paper did not filter low-count genes before normalisation (nor do they mention such action), so we used the raw counts to identify them. Genes with consistently low read counts were removed to reduce their influence on the analysis: only genes with at least 10 counts in a minimum of 80 samples were retained

```{r}
clean_counts_raw_df <- counts_raw_df |>
  filter(rowSums(across(-1) >= 10) >= 80)
```

We use `semi_join()` to remove the same genes from the normalised data. This function keeps only the rows of counts_norm whose gene_id also appears in the filtered raw data, without adding any columns from it.

```{r}
clean_counts_norm_df <- counts_norm_df |>
  semi_join(clean_counts_raw_df, by = "gene_id")
```

Exporting the clean normalised data

```{r}
write_tsv(x = clean_counts_norm_df, file = "data/02_counts_norm_clean.tsv")
```

## Augment Data

### Normalised Counts data

The dataset was transformed from wide to long format using `pivot_longer()`. This structure facilitates the integration of the count data with the sample metadata and supports subsequent exploratory analysis and visualization.

```{r}
counts_norm_long <- clean_counts_norm_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -gene_id,
    names_to  = "sample_id",
    values_to = "log2_counts")

counts_norm_long |>
  slice_sample(n=10)
```

### Creating one data set from two data sets

The two datasets were merged using the `sample_id` column as a common identifier. The `inner_join()` was used to retain only the samples present in both datasets, ensuring that each gene count was associated with its corresponding sample information.

```{r}
merged_data <- counts_norm_long|>
  inner_join(clean_sample_meta, by = "sample_id")

merged_data |>
  slice_sample(n = 10)
```

### Consistency in sample_id naming

```{r}
merged_data |>
  distinct(sample_id, replicate) |>
  count(replicate)
```

```{r}
merged_data <- merged_data |>
  mutate(sample_id = str_remove(sample_id, "_2"))
```

Export the augmented data

```{r}
write_tsv(x = merged_data, file = "data/02_aug_data.tsv")
```

## Organization of Data

To facilitate the analysis of gene expression at the individual gene level, the merged_data was grouped by `gene_id` and converted into a nested structure using `nest()`. This creates one row per gene, with all corresponding observations, regarding sample_id, counts and information about the donor, stored in a nested tibble.

```{r}
merged_data_nested <- merged_data |>
  select(c("gene_id","sample_id","log2_counts","condition_name","condition","sex")) |>
  group_by(gene_id) |>
  nest() |>
  ungroup()

merged_data_nested
```

To obtain an overview of gene expression across the different experimental conditions, descriptive statistics were calculated for each gene within each condition. The data were grouped by `gene_id` and `condition_name`, and the mean and standard deviation of the read counts were calculated. This provides an overview of the average expression levels and variability between samples for each gene and condition. Finally, missing values were removed to ensure that the resulting summary dataset contains valid statistical measurements.

```{r}
gene_summary <- merged_data |>
  group_by(gene_id, condition_name) |>
  summarise(
    mean_counts = mean(log2_counts),
    sd_log2_counts   = sd(log2_counts),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  drop_na()

gene_summary|>
  slice_sample(n= 10)
```

```{r}
dim(gene_summary)

n_distinct(gene_summary$gene_id)
```

### 2. PCA

```{r}
merged_data_PCA <- merged_data |>
  select(c("gene_id","sample_id","log2_counts", "condition_name")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = gene_id, values_from = log2_counts)

merged_data_PCA
```

```{r}
pca_fit <- merged_data_PCA |> 
  select(where(is.numeric)) |>  
  prcomp(scale = TRUE) 
```

```{r}
library("broom")
pca_fit |> 
  augment(merged_data_PCA) |>  
  ggplot(aes(.fittedPC1, .fittedPC2, color = condition_name)) + 
  geom_point(size = 1.5)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(factoextra)

fviz_pca_ind(
  pca_fit,
  geom.ind = "point",
  col.ind = merged_data_PCA$condition_name,
  palette = "jco",
  addEllipses = TRUE,
  ellipse.level = 0.95,
  legend.title = "Condition"
) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "PCA Plot Mapping the 4 conditions",
    subtitle = "Projection of samples onto PC1 and PC2",
    caption = "Plot Design (used on Lab07) from \nhttps://www.r-bloggers.com/2026/06/pca-in-r-principal-component-analysis-step-by-step-prcomp-ggplot2/#google_vignette"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8, color = "gray30")
  )

```
